```{r,echo=FALSE,message=FALSE,warning=FALSE,results='hide'}
library(tidyverse)
library(magrittr)   # needed for %T>% and %$%
library(nycflights13)
set.seed(42)
```

**Make sure `tidyverse`, `magrittr` and `nycflights13` are loaded** (`library(tidyverse); library(magrittr); library(nycflights13)`).

# Introduction

Welcome to the hands-on workshop "Tidy Work in Tidyverse". Most of the things necessary to complete the tutorials and challenges were covered in the lecture. However, sometimes the tasks require that you check the docs or search online. Not all our solutions are optimal. Let us know if you can do better or solve things in a different way. If stuck, look at hints, next google and if still stuck, turn to TA. It is a lot of material; sections marked **Stretch** are optional, do not feel bad if you do not solve all tasks. Good luck!

# Pipes

- Rewrite the following code chunk as one pipe (`magrittr`):

```{r,eval=FALSE}
my_cars <- mtcars[, c(1:4, 7)]
my_cars <- my_cars[my_cars$disp > mean(my_cars$disp), ]
print(my_cars)
my_cars <- colMeans(my_cars)
```

```{r, accordion=TRUE, echo=TRUE, eval=FALSE}
my_cars <- mtcars %>%
  select(c(1:4, 7)) %>%
  filter(disp > mean(disp)) %T>%
  print() %>%
  colMeans()
```

- Rewrite the correlations below using pipes.

```{r,eval=FALSE}
cor(mtcars)
```

```{r, accordion=TRUE, echo=TRUE, eval=FALSE}
mtcars %>% cor()
```

<details>
  <summary><strong>Tip?</strong></summary>
  You need to use different pipe for  this one. (Check the cheatsheet at the end of the lab). 
</details>
```{r,eval=FALSE}
cor(mtcars$gear, mtcars$mpg)
```

```{r, accordion=TRUE, echo=TRUE, eval=FALSE}
mtcars %$% cor(gear, mpg)
```

# Tibbles

- Convert the `mtcars` dataset to a tibble `vehicles`.

```{r,accordion=TRUE}
vehicles <- mtcars %>% as_tibble()
```

- Select the number of cylinders (`cyl`) variable using:
    - the `[[index]]` accessor,
    - the `[[string]]` accessor,
    - the `$` accessor.
    
```{r,accordion=TRUE}
vehicles[['cyl']]
vehicles[[2]]
vehicles$cyl
```

- Do the same selection as above, but using pipe and placeholders (use all three ways of accessing a variable).  

<details>
  <summary><strong>Tip?</strong></summary>
  1 - Which pipe allows you to print something but still pass **the original data forward**?  
  A. `%>%`  
  B. `%T>%`  
  C. `%$%`  
  D. `|>`  
  
  2 — Inside a pipe, which symbol refers to the current dataset?  
  A.` $`  
  B. `{}`  
  C. `.`  
  D. `_`  
  
  3 — Which structure lets you group multiple commands inside a pipe step?  
  A. `()` 
  B. `{ ... }`  
  C. `[]` 
  D. `<>`  
  
  4 — Which extraction matches `vehicles[['cyl']]`?  
  A. `.[2]`  
  B. `.$cyl`  
  C. `.[['cyl']]`  
  D. `[[2]]`  
  
  5 — Which pipeline ending would extract the `cyl` column from the data?  
  A. `%>% .$cyl`  
  B. `%T>% cyl`   
  C. `%>% cyl(.)`  
  D. `%$% cyl`  
</details>
```{r,accordion=TRUE}
vehicles %T>%
  {print(.[['cyl']])} %T>%
  {print(.[[2]])} %>%
  .$cyl
```

- Print the tibble.

```{r,accordion=TRUE}
vehicles
```

- Print the 30 first rows of the tibble.

```{r,accordion=TRUE}
vehicles %>% head(n = 30)
```

- Change the default behaviour of printing a tibble so that at least 15 and at most 30 rows are printed.

```{r,accordion=TRUE}
options(tibble.print_min = 15, tibble.print_max = 30)
```

- Convert `vehicles` back to a `data.frame` called `automobiles`.

```{r,accordion=TRUE}
automobiles <- as.data.frame(vehicles)
```

**Stretch:** can a column of a tibble refer to a column defined just before it? Try to create a tibble with `x` (10 random integers 1-10) and `y = log10(x)`. Does the same work in `data.frame()`?

```{r,accordion=TRUE}
tibble(x = sample(1:10, size = 10, replace = T), y = log10(x))
# data.frame(x = 1:3, y = log10(x)) fails: x is not found
```

**`tibble()` builds columns one after another, so later columns can use earlier ones.**


# NYC flights Challenge

The `nycflights13` package contains information about all flights that departed from NYC (i.e., EWR, JFK and LGA) in 2013: 336,776 flights with 16 variables. To help understand what causes delays, it also includes a number of other useful datasets: weather, planes, airports, airlines. We will use it to train working with tibbles and `dplyr`.

## Selecting columns

- Load the `nycflights13` package (install if necessary)

```{r,accordion=TRUE,eval=FALSE}
install.packages('nycflights13')
library(nycflights13)
```

- Read about the data in the package docs

```{r,accordion=TRUE,eval=FALSE}
?nycflights13
```

- Inspect the `flights` tibble.

```{r,accordion=TRUE}
flights
```

- Select all columns but `carrier` and `arr_time`

```{r,accordion=TRUE}
flights %>% select(-carrier, -arr_time)
```

- Select `carrier`, `tailnum` and `origin`

```{r,accordion=TRUE}
flights %>% select(carrier, tailnum, origin)
```

- Hide columns from `day` through `carrier`

```{r,accordion=TRUE}
flights %>% select(-(day:carrier))
```

- Select all columns that have to do with arrival (`arr_`) (hint: `contains`, `starts_with`, `matches`, `ends_with`; more details [here](https://dplyr.tidyverse.org/reference/select.html))  

```{r,accordion=TRUE}
flights %>% select(contains('arr_'))
```

- Select columns based on a vector `v <- c("arr_time", "sched_arr_time", "arr_delay")`

```{r,accordion=TRUE}
v <- c("arr_time", "sched_arr_time", "arr_delay")
flights %>% select(all_of(v))
# select(one_of(v)) is the older (superseded) way
```

- Rename column `dest` to `destination` using `select()` and `rename()`. What is the difference between the two approaches?

```{r,accordion=TRUE}
flights %>% select(destination = dest) %>% head()
flights %>% rename(destination = dest) %>% head()
# select keeps only the renamed column while rename returns the whole dataset
# with the column renamed
```

## Filtering rows

- Filter only the flights that arrived ahead of schedule

```{r,accordion=TRUE}
flights %>% filter(arr_delay < 0)
```

- Filter the flights that had departure delay between 10 and 33

```{r,accordion=TRUE}
flights %>% filter(dep_delay >= 10, dep_delay <= 33) # or
flights %>% filter(between(dep_delay, 10, 33))
```

- Fish out all flights with unknown arrival time

```{r,accordion=TRUE}
flights %>% filter(is.na(arr_time))
```

- Retrieve rows 1234:1258 (hint: `?slice`)

```{r,accordion=TRUE}
flights %>% slice(1234:1258)
```

- Sample (`?slice_sample()`) 3 random flights per day in March

```{r,accordion=TRUE}
flights %>% filter(month == 3) %>%
  group_by(day) %>%
  slice_sample(n = 3)
# older: sample_n(3)
```

- Show 5 most departure-delayed flights in January per carrier

```{r,accordion=TRUE}
flights %>%
  filter(month == 1) %>%
  group_by(carrier) %>%
  slice_max(dep_delay, n = 5)
# older: top_n(5, dep_delay)
```

- How many unique routes exists?

```{r,accordion=TRUE}
flights %>%
  mutate(route=paste(origin,"-",dest)) %>%
  distinct(route,.keep_all=T) %>%
  nrow()
```

- Which is the most frequent route?

```{r,accordion=TRUE}
flights %>%
  mutate(route=paste(origin,"-",dest)) %>% 
  count(route, sort = TRUE)

# JFK - LAX
```

## Trans(mutations)

- `air_time` is the amount of time in minutes spent in the air. Add a new column `air_spd` that will contain aircraft's airspeed in mph

```{r,accordion=TRUE}
flights %>% mutate(air_spd = distance/(air_time / 60))
```

- As above, but keep only the new `air_spd` variable

```{r,accordion=TRUE}
flights %>% transmute(air_spd = distance/(air_time / 60))
```

## Groups and counts

- Use `group_by()`, `summarise()` and `n()` to see how many planes were delayed (departure) every month

```{r,accordion=TRUE}
flights %>%
  filter(dep_delay > 0) %>%
  group_by(month) %>%
  summarise(num_dep_delayed = n())
```

- What was the mean `dep_delay` per month?

```{r,accordion=TRUE}
flights %>%
  group_by(month) %>%
  summarise(mean_dep_delay = mean(dep_delay, na.rm = T))
```

- Count the number of incoming delayed flights from each unique origin and sort origins by this count (descending)

```{r,accordion=TRUE}
flights %>%
  filter(arr_delay > 0) %>%
  group_by(origin) %>%
  summarise(cnt = n()) %>%
  arrange(desc(cnt))
```

- Use `summarise()` to sum total `dep_delay` per month in hours

```{r,accordion=TRUE}
 flights %>%
   group_by(month) %>%
   summarize(tot_dep_delay = sum(dep_delay/60, na.rm = T))
```

- Run `group_size()` on `carrier` what does it return?

```{r,accordion=TRUE}
flights %>%
    group_by(carrier) %>%
    group_size()
```

- Use `n_groups()` to check the number of unique origin-carrier pairs,

```{r,accordion=TRUE}
flights %>%
    group_by(carrier, origin) %>% 
  n_groups()
```

**Note on `ungroup`** Depending on the version of `dplyr` you may or may need to use the `ungroup()` if you want to group your data on some other variables. In the newer versions, `summarise` and `mutate` drop one aggregation level.


## More transformations

- Create a variable `delay_class` with `case_when()`: `"early"` if `dep_delay` < 0, `"on time"` if 0-15, `"late"` otherwise. Count flights per class.

```{r,accordion=TRUE}
flights %>%
  filter(!is.na(dep_delay)) %>%
  mutate(delay_class = case_when(dep_delay < 0 ~ "early",
                                 dep_delay <= 15 ~ "on time",
                                 .default = "late")) %>%
  count(delay_class)
```

- **Stretch:** use `across()` to compute the mean of `dep_delay` and `arr_delay` per `origin` in one `summarise()`.

```{r,accordion=TRUE}
flights %>%
  group_by(origin) %>%
  summarise(across(ends_with("_delay"), ~ mean(.x, na.rm = TRUE)))
```

# Joins

The `flights` table only has a two-letter `carrier` code. The `airlines`, `planes` and `airports` tables hold the details.

- Add the full airline `name` to `flights` (`left_join`). Which airline has the largest mean departure delay?

```{r,accordion=TRUE}
flights %>%
  left_join(airlines, by = "carrier") %>%
  group_by(name) %>%
  summarise(mean_dep_delay = mean(dep_delay, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  arrange(desc(mean_dep_delay))
```

- Which flights have no information in the `planes` table? (hint: `anti_join`). How many distinct `tailnum` is that?

```{r,accordion=TRUE}
flights %>% anti_join(planes, by = "tailnum") %>% distinct(tailnum) %>% nrow()
```

- **Stretch:** the key of `airports` is called `faa`, not `dest`. Join the destination airport names to `flights` and list the 5 most frequent destinations by name. (hint: `by = c("dest" = "faa")`)

```{r,accordion=TRUE}
flights %>%
  count(dest) %>%
  left_join(airports, by = c("dest" = "faa")) %>%
  select(dest, name, n) %>%
  slice_max(n, n = 5)
```

# Tidy data

- Look at `table1`, `table2`, `table3` and `table4a`/`table4b` (all in `tidyr`). Which one is tidy? Why are the others not?

```{r,accordion=TRUE}
table1
# table1 is tidy: one row per country-year, one column per variable.
# table2: a variable (type) is spread across rows; table3: `rate` holds two values;
# table4a/4b: the year (a value) is in column names.
```

- Make `table4a` tidy (hint: `pivot_longer`).

```{r,accordion=TRUE}
table4a %>% pivot_longer(c(`1999`, `2000`), names_to = "year", values_to = "cases")
```

- Make `table2` tidy (hint: `pivot_wider`).

```{r,accordion=TRUE}
table2 %>% pivot_wider(names_from = type, values_from = count)
```

- Split `rate` in `table3` into `cases` and `population` (hint: `separate`, `convert = TRUE`), then unite `country` and `year` into one column with `unite`.

```{r,accordion=TRUE}
table3 %>%
  separate(rate, into = c("cases", "population"), sep = "/", convert = TRUE) %>%
  unite("country_year", country, year, sep = "_")
```

# Stretch: capstone

For each origin airport, find the carrier with the highest mean departure delay among carriers with at least 100 flights from that origin. Report the airline's full name.

```{r,accordion=TRUE}
flights %>%
  group_by(origin, carrier) %>%
  summarise(n = n(), mean_dep_delay = mean(dep_delay, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
  filter(n >= 100) %>%
  group_by(origin) %>%
  slice_max(mean_dep_delay, n = 1) %>%
  left_join(airlines, by = "carrier")
```

# Cheatsheet  
## Pipe 
**Make sure to load the relevant libraries**. 

| Operator | Package | Short Explanation | Example |
|----------|------|-------------------|---------|
| `%>%` | **magrittr / tidyverse** | Forward pipe: passes the LHS as the **first argument** of the RHS function. Improves readability. | `mtcars %>% head(3)` |
| `%$%` | **magrittr** | Exposition pipe: **unpacks columns** of a data frame so they can be used directly inside a function. | `mtcars %$% cor(mpg, hp)` |
| `%T>%` | **magrittr** | Tee pipe: runs a function **for side effects** (e.g., plotting) but **returns the original data**. | `mtcars %T>% print() %>% summary()` |
| `\|>` | **base R** (R 4.1+) | Base pipe: similar to `%>%` but **stricter and simpler**. LHS is inserted into `_` placeholder if used. | `mtcars \|> head(3)` or `mtcars \|> (\(x) x[1:3, ])()` |


## Placeholder  

| Placeholder | Package | Used With | Short Explanation | Example |
|-------------|------|-----------|-------------------|---------|
| `.` | magrittr | `%>%` pipes | Insert LHS **anywhere** inside the RHS expression. | `mtcars %>% filter(mpg > mean(.$mpg))` |
| `.x` | purrr | `map()`, `walk()`, etc. | Represents the **current element** in purrr mapping. | `map(1:3, ~ .x^2)` |
| `.y` | purrr | `imap()` | Represents the **index/name** of the current element. | `imap(letters[1:3], ~ paste(.y, .x))` |
| `_` | base R | `\|>` | Base-R placeholder: places the LHS at a **named argument**. | `mtcars \|> lm(mpg ~ hp, data = _)` |



## Common dplyr, tidyr and tibble functions  

| Package | Function                      | What it does (short)                                                   | Tiny example                                                        |
| ------- | ----------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| dplyr   | `filter()`                    | Keep **rows** that satisfy one or more logical conditions.             | `flights %>% filter(dep_delay > 60)`                                |
| dplyr   | `select()`                    | Select or reorder **columns** by name, range, or helper functions.     | `flights %>% select(year, month, day, dep_delay)`                   |
| dplyr   | `mutate()`                    | Add or modify columns while keeping all existing columns.              | `flights %>% mutate(speed = distance / (air_time / 60))`            |
| dplyr   | `transmute()`                 | Like `mutate()`, but **drops all other columns**, keeps only new ones. | `flights %>% transmute(speed = distance / (air_time / 60))`         |
| dplyr   | `arrange()`                   | Reorder rows by one or more columns.                                   | `flights %>% arrange(dep_delay)`                                    |
| dplyr   | `arrange()` + `desc()`        | Sort rows in **descending** order of a variable.                       | `flights %>% arrange(desc(dep_delay))`                              |
| dplyr   | `group_by()`                  | Define groups of rows for grouped operations (e.g. summarise).         | `flights %>% group_by(carrier)`                                     |
| dplyr   | `summarise()` / `summarize()` | Collapse each group to **one row** with summary stats.                 | `flights %>% summarise(mean_delay = mean(dep_delay, na.rm = TRUE))` |
| dplyr   | `distinct()`                  | Return unique rows based on selected columns.                          | `flights %>% distinct(carrier)`                                     |
| dplyr   | `count()`                     | Shortcut for `group_by(...) %>% summarise(n = n())`.                   | `flights %>% count(carrier)`                                        |
| dplyr   | `slice()`                     | Select rows by position (row numbers).                                 | `flights %>% slice(1:5)`                                            |
| dplyr   | `slice_sample()`              | Randomly sample rows (replaces `sample_n()`).                          | `flights %>% slice_sample(n = 10)`                                  |
| dplyr   | `slice_max()` / `slice_min()` | Keep the rows with the largest / smallest values (per group if grouped); replaces `top_n()`. | `flights %>% slice_max(dep_delay, n = 5)`     |
| dplyr   | `rename()`                    | Rename columns while keeping all data.                                 | `flights %>% rename(delay = dep_delay)`                             |
| dplyr   | `desc()`         | Marks a variable for descending order in `arrange()` or `top_n()`.       | `flights %>% arrange(desc(dep_delay))`                                                      |
| dplyr   | `between()`      | Test if values lie between two endpoints (inclusive).                    | `flights %>% filter(between(dep_delay, 10, 30))`                                            |
| dplyr   | `everything()`   | Helper to select all remaining columns after those named.                | `flights %>% select(year, month, day, everything())`                                        |
| dplyr   | `contains()`     | Select columns whose names contain a given string.                       | `flights %>% select(contains("delay"))`                                                     |
| dplyr   | `all_of()`       | Select columns using a character vector of column names (replaces `one_of()`). | `vars <- c("year", "month"); flights %>% select(all_of(vars))`                        |
| dplyr   | `relocate()`     | Move columns, by default to the front.                                   | `flights %>% relocate(carrier)`                                                             |
| dplyr   | `case_when()`    | Vectorised if/else-if for several conditions.                            | `mutate(cls = case_when(dep_delay < 0 ~ "early", .default = "late"))`                       |
| dplyr   | `across()`       | Apply a function to several columns inside `mutate`/`summarise`.         | `summarise(across(ends_with("delay"), ~ mean(.x, na.rm = TRUE)))`                           |
| dplyr   | `.by`            | Group for one operation only (dplyr >= 1.1).                             | `flights %>% summarise(m = mean(dep_delay, na.rm = TRUE), .by = origin)`                    |
| dplyr   | `group_size()`   | Returns the size (row count) of each group for a grouped data frame.     | `flights %>% group_by(carrier) %>% group_size()`                                            |
| dplyr   | `n_groups()`     | Number of groups in a grouped data frame.                                | `flights %>% group_by(carrier) %>% n_groups()`                                              |
| dplyr   | `inner_join()`   | Join two data frames, keeping rows that match in both tables.            | `inner_join(df1, df2, by = "id")`                                                           |
| dplyr   | `left_join()`    | Keep all rows of the left table, add matching columns from the right.    | `left_join(flights, airlines, by = "carrier")`                                               |
| dplyr   | `anti_join()`    | Rows of the left table with **no** match in the right table.             | `anti_join(flights, planes, by = "tailnum")`                                                |
| dplyr   | `join_by()`      | Specify join keys, also with different names.                            | `left_join(x, y, by = join_by(id == key))`                                                  |
| tidyr   | `gather()`       | (Superseded, use `pivot_longer()`) Convert wide columns into key–value **long** format.        | `flights %>% gather(type, delay, dep_delay, arr_delay)`                                     |
| tidyr   | `pivot_longer()` | Modern replacement for `gather()`: wide → long.                          | `flights %>% pivot_longer(c(dep_delay, arr_delay), names_to = "type", values_to = "delay")` |
| tidyr   | `pivot_wider()`  | Long → wide, turning values of a column into new columns.                | `delays %>% pivot_wider(names_from = type, values_from = delay)`                            |
| tidyr   | `separate()`     | Split one column into multiple columns.                                  | `df %>% separate(col = "x_y", into = c("x","y"), sep = "_")`                                |
| tidyr   | `unite()`        | Combine multiple columns into a single one.                              | `df %>% unite("x_y", x, y, sep = "_")`                                                      |
| tidyr   | `complete()`     | Ensure all combinations of given variables exist (fill in missing rows). | `df %>% complete(year, month)`                                                              |
| tibble  | `as_tibble()`    | Convert an existing object (e.g. data.frame) into a tibble.              | `as_tibble(df)`                                                                             |
| tibble  | `tibble()`       | Create a tibble (modern data frame) from scratch.                        | `tibble(x = 1:3, y = letters[1:3])`                                                         |
